nodes.text: Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ and $D(A)$ be the set of those numbers which occur infinitely often as $a_1-a_2$ with $a_1,a_2\in A$. What conditions on $A$ are sufficient to ensure $D(A)$ has bounded gaps?

#332 : [ErGr80,p.50] number theory Prikry, Tijdeman, Stewart, and others (see the survey articles [St78] and [Ti79] ) have shown that a sufficient condition is that $A$ has positive density. One can also ask what conditions are sufficient for $D(A)$ to have positive density, or for $\sum_{d\in D(A)}\frac{1}{d}=\infty$, or even just $D(A)\neq\emptyset$.
